html:
The Guachichil were a nomadic Indigenous people of north central Mexico, the largest of the peoples the Aztecs and Spanish called Chichimecas. Their lands covered much of today's Zacatecas, San Luis Potosí and Guanajuato.

They lived by hunting, gathering mesquite pods, prickly pears and agave, and moving with the seasons. When silver was found at Zacatecas in 1546, Spanish roads and wagon trains crossed their land, and they fought back in the Chichimeca War of about 1550 to 1590, alongside the Zacatecos and others.

Spain finally won peace by paying them in food and cloth and by settling allied Tlaxcalan families among them. Within a few generations the Guachichil had been absorbed. See also the Guachichiles on the later map.
